newsitem.title: UK: LCE cocoa ends sharply down, crop talk cited.
newsitem.headline: LCE cocoa ends sharply down, crop talk cited.

text.p: London cocoa futures staged sharp losses on Tuesday as the key December contract slipped below 1,000 stg on origin selling and long liquidation.
Traders said talk that one U.S. crop forecaster has raised its profile for Ivory Coast was fuelling the bearish tone, while buyers were mostly sidelined.
There was no confirmation of the report, said to be published by Hans Kilian, but traders said it pointed to a range of 790,000-930,000 tonnes for the main Ivorian crop in 1996/97.
It was not clear whether the range, which traders saw as signalling an improvement in the crop, included the mid-crop carryover from 1995/96.
"As a forecasting range it's pretty wide," commented one crop analyst on the Kilian forecast.
He added that if carryover was not included, the big tail to the mid crop this year would add another 60,000 tonnes to the range.
LCE contracts saw nervous dealings on Tuesday, pressurised by New York's weak performance on Monday when London was closed for a Bank holiday.
The benchmark December contract slipped though a sequence of support points to touch a session low of 996 stg, but closed off the low at 999 stg, down 19 stg on the day.
September, gearing up to its first tender day next Monday, ended 23 stg lower at 973 stg.
Turnover totalled 5,539 lots, including AAs and crosses.
The Sept/Dec spread traded from 20 stg up to 25 stg while Dec/March was reasonably active at 11-12 stg, traders said.
Crop analysts said while the good survival of crops had improved the prospects for Ivory Coast after the heavy July rains, new setting was not impressive.
Traders were awaiting the next update from the UK pod counter Robert Fish, expected this week.
"People are hanging on to what's he going to say," said one trader.
Technically, cocoa is in for further losses after upside chances were exhausted last week when an earlier rally stalled and December returned to the low end of the previous range.
